items.description: Where the support is and how far it extends is only shown in Fig. 1 ('standard setup for the cantilever benchmark'). The text only mentions 'the Dirichlet boundary condition' (Sec. 3.5) and designs symmetric about mid-height (Sec. 3.4). That implies a symmetric support on the left (short) edge, but this is never stated.
readings: Entire left edge x = 0, 0 <= y <= H (H = 10)
Central segment of the left edge only (e.g. middle 50% of H)
Two short segments at the top and bottom ends of the left edge

items.description: The text never says which displacement components are fixed. 'Cantilever' suggests a full clamp, but only Fig. 1 shows the support type.
readings: Fully clamped: u_x = u_y = 0 at all support nodes
u_x = 0 along the support plus u_y = 0 at a single point (roller + pin)

items.entity: External load t0 at the free end
items.description: The load location is only shown in Fig. 1. Sec. 3.4 plots only the bottom half 'exploiting the symmetry of the designs', which points to a load at mid-height of the right (free) edge, but no position is stated.
readings: Right edge x = L at mid-height y = 0.5H
Right edge, bottom corner y = 0
Right edge, top corner y = H

items.entity: Traction t0 on the loaded boundary part
items.description: Eq. (1) writes the compliance as a boundary integral of u·t0 dA, i.e. a distributed traction. The text never gives the length of the loaded segment or says whether a nodal point load is used instead. A point load would make the compliance mesh-dependent.
readings: Nodal point load (zero length)
Uniform traction over a centred segment of length h0 = 1 (0.1H)
Uniform traction over a centred segment of length h2 = 0.25 (0.025H)
Uniform traction over the whole right edge (1.0H)

items.description: The text never states the load direction (only Fig. 1 shows it). A cantilever benchmark implies a transverse (vertical) load. The sign does not matter, since single-load compliance is quadratic in the load.
readings: Vertical (transverse to the beam axis), -y or +y (same layout and compliance)
Inclined load with a horizontal component (atypical for a cantilever)

items.description: No load magnitude is given in Eq. (1), Fig. 1 or Table 1. With E = 1 and unit thickness, a unit force on a 20x10 domain at V = 0.3 should give a compliance of order 10^2. The reported values (7.61e-5 in Fig. 2, 7.628e-5 in Sec. 4.3) are far smaller, which suggests a total force of order 1e-3.
readings: Total force F = 1
Unit traction |t0| = 1 over the loaded segment (F = segment length)
Small load, total F of about 1e-3 (inferred from the reported compliance)

items.description: The text neither specifies nor rules out passive regions. Whether Fig. 1 shows one, e.g. a solid pad under the load, cannot be checked.
readings: No passive regions; the whole 20x10 rectangle is designable
Small solid non-design pad at the load patch
Solid non-design strip along the supported edge

items.description: Table 1 lists 'E 1, μ 0.3'. μ usually denotes the shear modulus, while 0.3 is the typical value of Poisson's ratio. The text never names ν.
readings: Poisson's ratio ν = 0.3
Shear modulus μ = 0.3 with E = 1 (gives ν = E/(2μ) - 1 ≈ 0.667, admissible only as a 2D plane-stress material)

items.description: The text does not say whether the model is plane stress or plane strain. Sec. 2 treats ρ as the out-of-plane thickness of an extruded sheet, which implies plane stress.
readings: Plane stress (element stiffness proportional to thickness ρ)
Plane strain (effective ν = ν/(1-ν) ≈ 0.43, effective modulus E/(1-ν²))

items.description: The physical sheet thickness that ρ = 1 stands for is not given. It is needed for the 2D stiffness and for the absolute compliance value.
readings: Another value t0 (compliance scales as 1/t0)

items.description: Table 1 gives 'Filter type PDE, Radius 0.375 (1.5h2)' and cites Lazarov & Sigmund (2011). It does not say whether 0.375 is the length parameter r in -r²∇²ρ̃ + ρ̃ = ρ or the equivalent density-filter radius R, with r = R/(2√3). This matters when mapping the filter onto another solver's filter.
readings: Helmholtz parameter r = 0.375 used directly (≈ hat-filter radius 2√3·0.375 ≈ 1.30, i.e. 20.8 elements on a 320x160 grid)
0.375 is the equivalent hat/density-filter radius (Helmholtz r = 0.375/(2√3) ≈ 0.108; hat radius = 6 elements on 320x160)

items.description: Sec. 2 gives only the filter type and radius. It does not give the Helmholtz filter's boundary conditions or say how the filtered field is mapped to element densities (nodal Q1 values vs. element-wise).
readings: Homogeneous Neumann on the whole boundary (Lazarov & Sigmund default, volume-preserving)
Dirichlet or padded-domain boundary treatment

items.description: Sec. 2 / Table 1 give GOCM (Kim et al. 2021) with initial step length 0.05, decay 0.98 per iteration, minimum 1e-4 and an 'exponential' design update. Neither 'step length' nor 'exponential' is defined here; 'exponential' could mean a multiplicative update or the exponential step decay. The step reaches its floor after about 307 iterations, which may freeze a design that has not fully converged.
readings: GOCM with exponential (multiplicative) update, step 0.05·0.98^k bounded below by 1e-4
Standard OC with move limit 0.05 decayed by 0.98 per iteration (floor 1e-4)
MMA or another optimizer run to convergence (the p = 1 VTTO problem is convex)

items.description: Eq. (2) is a volume-weighted mean of Δρ_e. It does not say whether Δρ_e is an absolute value; a signed mean is about 0 whenever the volume constraint is active. It also doesn't say whether raw or filtered densities are used, and gives no maximum iteration count.
readings: Volume-weighted mean of |Δρ_e| of the raw design variables < 1e-4
Volume-weighted mean of |Δρ̃_e| of the filtered (physical) densities < 1e-4
Either of the above plus an iteration cap (value unspecified)

items.entity: Finite element mesh (adaptive vs. fixed grid)
items.description: The results use adaptive meshing: start at level 2 (80x40), levels 0-4, refine when the density jump exceeds 0.05 and coarsen when it is below 0.001. Adaptation frequency and data transfer are left to Stankiewicz et al. (2025b). Remark 1 says a fixed 320x160 grid has the same resolution, but does not claim identical results.
readings: Uniform 320x160 grid, h = 0.0625 (filter radius = 6 elements)
Uniform 80x40 grid, h = 0.25 (initial level; filter radius = 1.5 elements)
Adaptive 20x10 base mesh with levels 0-4 and the density-jump criteria (adaptation frequency unspecified)

items.description: Sec. 2 writes h4 = 1·0.5^4 = 0.06125, but 0.5^4 = 0.0625. Only 0.0625 is consistent with 320x160 cells on the 20x10 domain (80x40 at h2 = 0.25, Remark 1).
readings: h4 = 0.06125 as printed (320x160 cells would then span 19.6x9.8)

items.description: The element formulation is not stated; deal.II supports any polynomial order. The text only implies one density per quadrilateral cell.
readings: Bilinear 4-node quadrilaterals (Q1)
Biquadratic quadrilaterals (Q2)

items.description: Fig. 2 compares VTTO with 'standard SIMP-based TO', but Sec. 2 gives no penalty exponent, continuation or projection for the SIMP run. p = 3 appears only in Sec. 3.1 (low-thickness suppression), and c_p is never given a value.
readings: p = 3 fixed (modified SIMP, ρ_min = 1e-9), same PDE filter, no projection
p continued from 1 to 3 with a multiplicative factor c_p (value unspecified)
p = 3 plus a smoothed Heaviside projection

items.description: The Fig. 2 caption lists 7.61e-5 and 8.92e-5 'respectively' for SIMP and VTTO, which would make VTTO the worse design. The text says penalization raises compliance by 17.2% (8.92/7.61 = 1.172), and the VTTO reference in Sec. 4.3 (7.628e-5) matches 7.61e-5.
readings: VTTO = 7.61e-5, SIMP = 8.92e-5 (consistent with the text and Sec. 4.3)
VTTO = 8.92e-5, SIMP = 7.61e-5 (literal caption order)
